description:
PARKED — raised 2026-08-19, deliberately not scheduled. Recorded so the question is not lost.

cuneiform/362 is building a SAFETY-MODE vocabulary for the default export console: a declared posture (roughly ask-for-approval → approve-edits → plan-first → autonomous) that the runtime enforces and the run records, gating spend and irreversibility rather than every action. It is being built locally, in cuneiform, in a shape that could become a contract without being rewritten.

The question this tasklist holds: **should autonomy posture be a koine clause?**

The case for is the ownership boundary. Two organizations run products over this fabric, and the two edges that cross it — `talos → argos` (Tier-B/C A/V analysis) and `insimul → lugh` (world-derived SLM training) — are inter-organizational integrations. If Overpowered dispatches work to an Ontolo service, 'autonomous' has to mean the same thing on both sides, or the posture the caller believes it selected is not the posture the callee enforces. That is exactly the class of problem koine exists for, and it is why the role-scoped, product-agnostic clause style is right here rather than fussy.

The case against is prematurity. One console's vocabulary is not yet evidence of a shared need, and a clause written before two independent implementations exist tends to encode the first one's accidents.

Do not start this until cuneiform/362 has shipped and a SECOND consumer wants the same vocabulary. Re-ask then.
verify: python3 -c "import json,glob; [json.load(open(f)) for f in glob.glob('schemas/*.json')]; print('schemas ok')"

userStories.title: Decide whether posture is a contract at all
acceptanceCriteria: An ADR answers it either way, with the cross-org edges named as the concrete case rather than argued in the abstract.
If the answer is no, the ADR says what would change the answer, and this tasklist is retired against it. A parked question with no closing condition is just a backlog entry.
The answer must account for the fact that the two edges cross an ownership boundary — a posture that is only advisory across that line provides no guarantee to either side.
userStories.notes: ADR-0013 written and Accepted (2026-08-26): answers YES-in-the-boundary-half, with the console ladder rejected (option c). AC1 — the two cross-owner edges are named concretely from ECOSYSTEM.md §3 (talos→argos Tier-B/C analysis, insimul→lugh corpora) and the decision is argued against them, not in the abstract. AC3 — advisory-across-the-line is answered head-on: measurement 1 greps all six specs and finds NO clause/field/enum naming irreversibility anywhere (spend is covered by KCB §5, so a posture gating 'spend and irreversibility' is inapplicable, not merely weak), and measurement 2 fixes that only the callee's unilateral gates plus the caller's narrowed grant bind across an ownership boundary — hence a monotone-restrictive intersection rule rather than a trusted mode flag. AC2 — the answer is not 'no', so the closing condition is stated in both directions: withdrawal triggers W1/W2/W3 are checkable, the parked second-implementation condition is retained as a ratification gate, and this tasklist is retired against the record. Guards: check-doc-integrity green (49 markdown files, 910 relative links checked, all 3 status tables match headers), check-schemas green, check-registry green, check-tasklist-categories green, schemas json-parse ok. No spec version moves.

userStories.title: If it is a clause, it is role-scoped and product-agnostic
acceptanceCriteria: The vocabulary names postures by what they GUARANTEE, not by what a particular console calls its buttons.
It states the floor — the stops no posture may skip — since that is the only part a caller can rely on when the callee is another organization.
A scenario covers a cross-org dispatch where caller and callee postures disagree, and states which wins.
It is expressible by an implementation that has no console at all.
userStories.notes: KCB 0.4.8 §4.3 written + the pressure leg scenarios/kcb-cross-owner-posture.md (426 lines, deltas AP-1…AP-8, blocking AP-5). AC1 — postures are named by GUARANTEE: §4.3b makes a posture a SET of admitted effect classes (reversibility x visibility), states that koine adopts NO rung names and defines NO total order, and makes a product ladder a projection with lossy edges named (ADR-0010's discipline); the console's four rungs appear nowhere in the clause. AC2 — the floor is §4.3d, normative and non-negotiable: no posture relaxes KGP §7, KCB §5 or KFT §4/§8.1; an unadmitted effect is a refusal, never a silent proceed or substitution; an undeclared class is not admitted; refusal always available to both sides. AC3 — Step 3 of the scenario is the cross-org disagreement (caller strict on permanence, callee strict on spend), tests four candidate rules and states which wins: the INTERSECTION governs, the restriction always wins, no arbitration and no trust needed (§4.3c) — and Step 4's blocking AP-5 found the pairwise rule evaporates on a delegated leg to a third owner, closed by §4.3e's chain rule. AC4 — Step 8 re-runs the whole leg headless and §4.3g is a NORMATIVE conformance requirement: no person, interface, timeout or approval message anywhere; a refused dispatch is not parked or resumable, a widened re-dispatch is a new invocation, so no verb or state is added. Guards: check-doc-integrity green (50 markdown files, 938 relative links checked, all 3 status tables match headers), check-schemas green, check-registry green, check-tasklist-categories green (5 tasklists), schemas json-parse ok, .chief/verify.sh green. Version moves 0.4.7 -> 0.4.8 (patch, every field optional); mirrors updated in README/specs-README/ECOSYSTEM/CLAUDE.md/ROADMAP/scenarios-README/decisions-README/ADR-0013 amendment log/governance map G5 (Partial narrow -> Partial). Cross-repo obligation recorded: this is the TWELFTH scenario against a downstream encoding set of nine, so agora's coverage set-equality test goes red — named in the scenario row, the scenario itself and ROADMAP.
